{{for|the women's rights author and principal|Jane F. Barry}}
{{Use Canadian English|date=January 2023}}

'''Pamela Jane Barry''' (born July 10, 1944) is a chemist and former politician in [[New Brunswick]]. She represented [[Saint John West (electoral district)|Saint John West]] and then [[Saint John Lancaster]] in the [[Legislative Assembly of New Brunswick]] from 1987 to 1999 as a [[Liberal Party of New Brunswick|Liberal]] member.

==Biography==

===Early years===
She was born in [[City of Halifax|Halifax, Nova Scotia]] and was educated at [[Mount St. Vincent University]] and [[Saint Francis Xavier University]], receiving a [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]]

===Career===
Barry worked as a chemist for [[Lantic Sugar Limited]] and as a research assistant at the [[University of Alberta]] Faculty of Pharmacy. She served in the province's Executive Council as Minister of State for Childhood Services, [[Department of Environment (New Brunswick)|Minister of the Environment]] and [[Solicitor General (New Brunswick)|Solicitor General]]. Barry was defeated in the 1999 general election.

From 2000 to 2011, Barry was the executive director of The Greater Saint John Community Foundation.
